newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps - Steady in rudderless trade.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps - Steady in rudderless trade.

text.p: Singapore oil product swaps were steady in lacklustre trading as the market drifted in the absence of fresh regional indicators and steady overnight crude values, traders said.
"The market is not going anywhere right now. There's not much volatility and trading is thin," one trader said.
September gas oil was last quoted unchanged from Monday at $23.10/$23.20 per barrel with no trades seen, brokers said.
It traded several times within a tight 10-cent band on Monday at between $21.10 and $21.20 per barrel, they said.

Traders said sentiment remain bearish because no fresh incremental buying has emerged from the region as most importing countries, such as China, have high stocks and are raising domestic output in an effort to cutback imports.

But the shutdown of the bigger 200,000-barrel-per-day (bpd) Cilacap's crude unit in October for up to three months is expected to keep Indonesian monthly imports of middle distillate at the higher end of its range, traders said.
Traders estimate gas oil import to reach at least five million barrels and jet fuel at two million barrels.
Cilacap's 100,000-bpd crude unit is currently undergoing a 35-day beginning August 12.
The current poor demand was again reflected in the spot physical market where a 200,000-barrel cargo traded at 40 cents below spot Singapore quotes, free-on-board basis.
The cargo was offered at a 30-cent discount in the past week but no buyers emerged.
Singapore fuel oil swaps are steady after physical players emerged on Monday to draw up the trading boundaries. The physical market was bid and offered at between $103 and $105 per tonne.
September fuel oil swaps were last quoted 25 cents lower from Monday at $103.50/$104.25 per tonne with October up 50 cents at $104.25/$105.00, brokers said.
September traded on Monday at $104.00 and October at $104.50, they said.
